title: German Grammar Review — B1 to C2
scope: Grammar only: morphology, syntax, verb forms, case, word order and sentence combining. Vocabulary, idioms and pronunciation are handled elsewhere.
sources: telc Grammatiktraining Deutsch für B2 — official table of contents
telc Grammatiktraining Deutsch für A1–B1 — official table of contents (Probekapitel)
Cornelsen Grammatik aktiv B2/C1 — chapter index
telc Deutsch C1 and C2 Übungstest format tables
CEFR Companion Volume 2020 — linguistic competence and propositional precision scales
caveats: No exam provider publishes a topic-by-topic grammar syllabus for C1 or C2. Goethe explicitly declines to fix a grammar or vocabulary inventory at those levels, so the C1 and C2 lists are inferred from coursebook canons and task formats.
Providers disagree on level placement. Topics marked provider_split are contested; the note gives the split.
ÖSD specifications could not be retrieved in usable form, so no ÖSD claims are made.

topics.topic_en: Personal pronouns and the verb sein
topics.covers: ich, du, er, sie, es, wir, ihr, sie and the conjugation of sein.
subject forms and their use, including the polite Sie.
mich, dich, ihn, sie, es and which verbs take an accusative object.
der/die/das, ein/eine and kein as the negative article.
der → den, die → die, das → das with the case driving the ending.
der/die/das as gender markers, and the three plural forms.
the five plural types: -e, -en, -er, -n and zero.
der Hund / den Hund: only the masculine changes.
mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, ihr, Ihr as attributive possessives.
dieser, jener, jeder, welcher — used alone without a noun.

topics.topic_en: Present tense: regular, -eln/-ern and vowel-changing verbs
topics.covers: the -e/-st/-t endings, the stem change in -eln/-ern verbs (sammeln, wandern), and vowel-consonant irregulars (nehmen → du nimmst, fahren → du fährst).
lesen → du liest, geben → du gibst, and the vowel-consonant pattern.
sammeln, wandern, and the silent-e rule.
stem form, no ending, and the e→i change: du nimmst!
durch, für, gegen, ohne, um and their fixed uses.
in, an, auf, über, unter, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen — the case is decided by wo? (location, dative) versus wohin? (movement, accusative).
aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu.
anrufen, aufstehen: the prefix goes to the end of the sentence.
be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ver-, zer- take no prefix change and no ge- in the Partizip.
sich freuen, sich waschen — accusative reflexive pronouns.
the most frequent modals and the infinitive that follows.

topics.topic_en: Verbs with separable prefixes and modals
topics.covers: anrufen → anrufen möchte: the verb cluster keeps the prefix inside.
ich mache, du machst, er macht — the regular present pattern.

topics.topic_en: Nouns in the plural after numbers
topics.covers: zwei Männer, drei Frauen, and the singular after eine.
das große Haus — the uninflected adjective as a first step.
hier, dort, wo and their use with sein.
heute, morgen, gestern, jetzt.
coordinating conjunctions joining main clauses, and their position in the sentence.
pointing things out and contrasting with jener.

topics.topic_en: Word order: the verb in second position
topics.covers: the conjugated verb in position II in every main clause.
wo, wohin, wann, wer, was, wie, warum put the verb in position II; yes-no questions put the verb in position I.
the politeness particle and its position before the main verb.
immer, oft, manchmal, nie and their placement before the verb.
erste, zweite … with the adjective ending; 1.–31. and the word order in spoken versus written dates, including der 5. Oktober 2026.
der 5. Oktober 2026 — spoken and written word order.
um, am, im and the preposition+article contractions.
nicht vs. kein: the two German negatives and their position.
mir, dir, ihm, ihnen / mich, dich, ihn, sie, es and their word order.
the full article in all four cases and the dem/den/das contractions.
im, am, zum, zur, vom, beim, ins, aufs and how they are read aloud.
dieser, jener, jeder, man and the identical die/das forms.
verbs of motion toward a person, and German's two-object rule.
schriftlich vor, telefonisch mit and the case each governs.
warten auf, helfen bei, sprechen über and the case they govern.
auf ihn, über sie and pronoun agreement with the preposition.
des Freundes, of people, places and measures.
während, trotz, wegen, statt.
der Name → den Namen, den Kollegen and the weak plural in -en.
das Museum → das Museum, and the plural in -n or -e.

topics.topic_en: Adjective declension after a definite article
topics.covers: weak endings in -e, and -en in the dative plural.

topics.topic_en: Adjective declension after an indefinite article
topics.covers: mixed endings: -er, -e, -es, -en.
strong endings and attributive versus predicative use.
mein, dein, sein take the same endings as ein.
viel, wenig, ein paar and the mixed/strong pattern they follow.
-er form, gut → besser, hoch → höher and the vowel change.
am besten, am höchsten and the -sten adjective ending.
so groß wie, genauso teuer wie.
das große Haus vs. das Haus ist groß — the decisive difference.

topics.topic_en: Perfect tense with sein and haben
topics.covers: sein for movement and change of state, haben otherwise.
war and hatte — the two irregular forms every learner must know.
ich machte, du machtest and the -te endings.
gehen → ging, sehen → sah, sprechen → sprach and the vowel change.
gegangen, gesehen and where the ge- goes.
be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, ver-, zer- take ge- inside the word.

topics.topic_en: Verbs changing the stem vowel in the past
topics.covers: nehmen → nahm, essen → aß, give the vowel change a special treatment.
müssen → müssen, können → können plus the bare infinitive.
verb-final and the comma before the subordinate clause.
wenn, als, bevor, nachdem, seit, bis.
weil, denn, deshalb, deshalb and sodass.
sein and werden as the two copulas of German.
krank werden, rot werden — werden marks a change, sein a state.

topics.topic_en: Infinitive with zu, and the fixed verbs without it
topics.covers: which verbs take zu, which fixed verbs omit it (sehen, hören, lassen, gehen), and where the infinitive stands.

topics.topic_en: Weil-clauses before and after the verb
topics.covers: weil-Sätze at position I or at the end, and the comma rule.
sich etwas vorstellen, sich etwas wünschen, es sich leisten — when the reflexive takes the dative.
Wir helfen uns gegenseitig / einander.

topics.topic_en: Konjunktiv II: würde forms and the own forms
topics.covers: ich würde, wir würden as the safe form, and the own forms of sein, haben and the modals that replace würde.
formal requests with the verb in position I.
used to replace und/oder after a negative.
verbfirst in the main clause, verb-second with the conjugated verb, verb-last in the subordinate clause.
the strictly-earlier layer of the past, and why it marks the earlier of two past events.
formation and word order of werden + Infinitiv, and reading it as prediction vs. spoken intention.

topics.topic_en: Modal verbs: conjugation and sentence pattern
topics.covers: the modal + infinitive pattern, and the position of the infinitive when another object follows.
sicher, wohl, vielleicht and the modal + inflected infinitive used as an adverb.
es gibt, es regnet, mir ist kalt: es as a formal placeholder subject.
Ich gebe ihm das Buch, and why the shorter dative object comes first.
du, ihr, Sie and the let-forms, including the position of the pronoun.

topics.topic_en: Adjective declension after an indefinite or possessive article
topics.term_de: Adjektivdeklination nach unbestimmten Artikeln und Possessiva
topics.covers: mixed endings: -er, -e, -es, -en, and the ein- irregularity.

topics.topic_en: Adjective declension with demonstratives and possessives
topics.covers: dieser/jener/ein jeder and the pattern they share.
-er, am -sten, Gleichstand, and ellipsis in the comparison.
gut → besser → am besten, and where adverb comparison differs from adjective comparison.

topics.topic_en: Participles I and II as adjectives
topics.term_de: Partizip I und II als Adjektiv
topics.covers: das kommende Jahr, das reparierte Auto: participle plus adjective ending.
der/die/das, welcher/welche/welches; case is decided inside the relative clause.

topics.topic_en: Relative clauses: dative, genitive and prepositions
topics.term_de: Relativsätze im Dativ, Genitiv und mit Präpositionen
topics.covers: deren, dessen, and relative pronouns after a preposition.

topics.topic_en: Relative clauses with was, wo, wohin, wann
topics.covers: weil sie Dinge und Personen ersetzen; wo vs. wohin vs. wann.
weil, da, denn, obwohl, trotzdem als Konjunktion.
damit, um zu, zu, sodass, so dass.
which verbs take zu, and the fixed verbs that omit it.
deshalb, trotzdem, außerdem: position zero, then verb in position II.
ob, wann, wo, wie, warum and the verb-final subordinate clause.
quotation marks, the colon, and pronoun and tense adjustment.
the umlaut + -e forms of sein, haben and the modals.

topics.topic_en: Konjunktiv II: wishes and polite requests
topics.term_de: Konjunktiv II für Wünsche und Höflichkeit
topics.covers: ich würde, gern hätte, könnte ich bitte — the everyday wish and request forms.
würde + haben/sein + Partizip II.

topics.term_de: Konjunktiv II für Ratschläge und Vorschläge
topics.covers: sollte, müsste and thewürde-form for proposing.
wenn + Konjunktiv II and the verb-final position of the wenn-clause.
werden + Partizip II across tenses, and the von-phrase agent.
müssen/sollen/können + werden + Partizip II, and the resulting meanings.

topics.term_de: sein + Partizip II vs. werden + Partizip II
topics.covers: result vs. process, and sein for the resultative reading.
der Name / der Kollege / das Museum: the full masculine and neuter paradigm with the special plurals.
topics.split_note: Recognition at B1, productive use at B2; telc introduces the full paradigm earlier.

topics.covers: every subordinate clause has the verb last; the conjunctions that introduce one, and the comma that always follows.
wenn/als in real conditions, plus ob and the ich-Passiv alternative.

topics.topic_en: so-clauses: so … wie and so … dass
topics.covers: comparison with so, and result with so … dass / sodass.
als ob, als wenn, als though for unreal resemblance.
der/die/das, welcher, deren, dessen and the case decided inside the relative clause.
the compressed subordinate clause: die zur Verfügung stehenden Daten.
zu + Partizip I + adjective ending agreeing with the following noun: die zu lösenden Aufgaben.

topics.topic_en: Narrating the past: Präteritum vs. Plusquamperfekt
topics.covers: which past tense carries the narrative, and using Plusquamperfekt for the earlier event.

wissen, glauben and modal meaning without an infinitive.
a modal inside a reported clause: Er sagt, er müsse arbeiten.

topics.topic_en: Modal verbs of deduction and hedging
topics.covers: müssen, dürfen, können expressing the speaker's degree of certainty.
the own forms of sein, haben and the modals, and when they replace würde.

topics.topic_en: Konjunktiv II in formal and official requests

an expression for what you hope will not happen.

topics.covers: er habe gesagt, and the identical 3rd-person-plural form.
